sections.normalized_html: One liter of varnish will cover [MATH: 150] square feet of a surface. A wooden patio has a total area of [MATH: P] square feet. Find an equation representing the total amount of varnish [MATH: S,] in liters, needed to varnish the patio three times.
sections.readable_text: One liter of varnish will cover [MATH: 150] square feet of a surface. A wooden patio has a total area of [MATH: P] square feet. Find an equation representing the total amount of varnish [MATH: S,] in liters, needed to varnish the patio three times.

sections.normalized_html:
Since one liter covers [MATH: 150] square feet, varnishing a patio of area [MATH: P] square feet once would require

[MATH: \frac{P}{150} \,\, \text{liters.}]

To varnish the patio three times, we simply triple this amount, so we get

[MATH: 3 \times \frac{P}{150} = \frac{P}{50}.]

Therefore, the equation that represents the total amount of varnish [MATH: S,] in liters, needed to varnish the patio of area [MATH: P] three times, is

[MATH: S = \frac{P}{50}.]
